Notice that `SCAN_SINGLE_FULLY_MASKED` passes `NULL` as the mask to `SCAN_TYPE`, so it doesn't add to the mask buffer. But `SCAN_END_SINGLE` calls `SCAN_PUT(ATTR, NULL)` which calls `SCAN_PUT_ATTR(key, ATTR, skey, FUNC)` and `SCAN_PUT_ATTR(mask, ATTR, smask, FUNC)` - so it DOES add to the mask buffer.

Wait, let me re-read `SCAN_PUT`:
```c
#define SCAN_PUT(ATTR, FUNC)                            \
        SCAN_PUT_ATTR(key, ATTR, skey, FUNC);           \
        if (mask)                                       \
            SCAN_PUT_ATTR(mask, ATTR, smask, FUNC);
```

In `parse_odp_key_mask_attr`, the `mask` parameter is the `struct ofpbuf *mask` passed to the function. So when called from `parse_odp_action`'s `set()` handler, `mask` is `&maskbuf` (non-NULL), so it WILL add to the mask buffer.

So the mask buffer should always have data added when `parse_odp_key_mask_attr` succeeds. Let me think about this differently...
